stories.title: Scientists are finding AI may make us remember things that never happened
stories.simple_summary: Scientists discovered that AI programs can accidentally make people remember events that never actually happened. This happens because the AI can suggest false details so convincingly that our brains accept them as real memories.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use AI to help you remember things, be careful. Don't assume everything it tells you is true. Always double-check important information.

stories.title: US Treasury pushes global partners to rename AI as 'super intelligence'
stories.simple_summary: The US Treasury Department is asking other countries to start calling AI by a new name: 'super intelligence' instead of just 'AI.' This is mostly a terminology change being negotiated at a government level.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to government officials and policymakers. It won't change how AI actually works or affects your daily life.

stories.title: AI agents are coming to Rivian’s cars
stories.simple_summary: Rivian, a car company, is adding AI assistants to their vehicles. These assistants will be able to help drivers with various tasks, though the full details won't be clear until December.
stories.why_it_matters: If you drive a Rivian or plan to buy one, future models may have a helpful AI assistant. For most people with other cars, this doesn't affect you yet.

stories.title: How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft and Nvidia are making laptops that run AI programs better, with Windows software specially tuned to work with them. These new RTX Spark laptops are designed to handle AI tasks more smoothly.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to engineers and people buying expensive new laptops for specialized work. If you have a regular laptop for email and web browsing, you don't need to worry about this.

stories.title: Google’s Universal Cart shopping tool launches in the US
stories.simple_summary: Google created a new online shopping tool that lets you add items from different stores to one cart. You can use it on Google Search or in the Gemini app starting now in the US.
stories.why_it_matters: If you shop online and use Google, this tool might make it easier to compare prices and checkout from multiple stores in one place. It's convenient but not essential.

stories.title: Nobody is safe from celebrity AI deepfakes
stories.simple_summary: AI can now create fake videos and images of celebrities doing and saying things they never did. These fake images look realistic enough to fool people on social media.
stories.why_it_matters: Be skeptical of images and videos you see online, especially if they seem surprising or embarrassing. They could be AI fakes. Don't share them without being sure they're real.

stories.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Last day
stories.simple_summary: This is an advertisement for a technology conference happening in 2026. It's a sales message for an event where tech professionals gather.
stories.why_it_matters: Unless you work in technology or are interested in attending a large industry conference, this doesn't affect you.

stories.title: Benn Jordan on Flock, privacy, and the new surveillance backlash
stories.simple_summary: This is an interview announcement with a researcher who investigates privacy and surveillance issues related to technology. The headline doesn't provide specific news about a new development.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're concerned about privacy online, this interview might provide useful insights. Otherwise, it's mostly content for people interested in media and tech trends.

stories.title: Google launches its ‘universal’ online shopping cart ahead of the holidays
stories.simple_summary: Google launched a shopping cart tool that works across different online stores. You can use it in Google Search or the Gemini app to make holiday shopping easier.
stories.why_it_matters: If you do online shopping during the holidays, this tool could save you time by letting you browse multiple stores in one place. It's optional and convenient but not necessary.

stories.title: Amazon introduces 2 new AI products from Bee: Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse
stories.simple_summary: Amazon's company called Bee released two new devices that use AI. These devices help with various tasks and connect to Alexa and Amazon services.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Amazon products and services, you may see these new AI devices offered to you. Otherwise, this is just a new product announcement from a major company.

stories.title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
stories.simple_summary: Amazon's Bee devices are small AI tools. One is a wearable you can wear, and one is a tiny recorder that clips to your phone. They listen to conversations, create lists, and help you shop, starting at about $75.
stories.why_it_matters: If you like Amazon's services and gadgets, these devices might interest you as affordable AI helpers. But they do record your conversations, so think carefully about privacy before buying.

stories.title: Amazon’s always-listening Bee wearable can now help you buy stuff
stories.simple_summary: Amazon sold updated versions of Bee devices that constantly listen and record what you say. The new models can help you remember conversations and shop on Amazon, costing around $75.
stories.why_it_matters: If privacy concerns you, be aware that these devices record your conversations. Only consider them if you're comfortable with that level of listening. For most people focused on privacy, these may not be right for you.
